prompt: Why can IR spectroscopy be used in real-time breathalyzer devices to monitor blood alcohol levels?

options.label: Ethanol absorbs strongly at a specific C–O frequency (~1050 cm⁻¹); absorbance is linear with concentration via Beer's law.
Ethanol fluoresces when exposed to infrared radiation, and the emission intensity scales with concentration.
IR measures the oxygen depletion caused by ethanol metabolism in the lungs, which correlates to BAC.
Ethanol's unique fingerprint region (below 1500 cm⁻¹) is pattern-matched against a reference library to quantify it.

explanation: IR breathalyzers lock onto ethanol's characteristic C–O stretch (~1050 cm⁻¹). Beer–Lambert makes absorbance linear with concentration; the breath/blood ratio (~2100:1) converts breath reading to BAC. Fluorescence (UV/Vis) and O₂ consumption don't apply here.
